key_insight: A systematic, multi-axis evaluation reveals that current image-manipulation localization methods fail inconsistently across different domains (editing tools, semantic content, and distribution shifts), exposing hidden brittleness that single-axis benchmarks miss.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of comprehensive, cross-domain evaluation for image-manipulation localization by providing a framework and benchmark that measures robustness and generalization across multiple real-world axes of variation.
method: Define multiple evaluation axes (e.g., editing tool/type, image domain/semantics, distribution shift, post-processing) to stress-test localization models.
Assemble or curate a benchmark dataset and standardized metrics for per-pixel localization performance under each axis and their combinations.
Run systematic, comparative experiments across state-of-the-art detectors to quantify failure modes, robustness gaps, and trade-offs.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical diagnostic toolkit and benchmark to choose, improve, and harden localization models for deployment; clarifies which models generalize across realistic manipulation scenarios and where targeted improvements are needed.
visual_elements: Axis diagram: radial or matrix layout showing evaluation axes (tool, domain, shift, post-processing) and how they combine.
Side-by-side image examples: original, manipulated, and model localization heatmaps to illustrate success vs. failure cases.
Bar/line charts: per-method performance across axes to highlight robustness gaps and ranking changes.
Failure-mode heatmap: matrix showing which combinations of axes cause most drop in localization (dark = large drop).
paper_title: Multi-axis Analysis of Image Manipulation Localization
paper_authors: Keanu Nichols, Divya Appapogu, Giscard Biamby, Dina Bashkirova, Anna Rohrbach
